rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This is a focused conceptual and problem-solving plan. It starts with the product rule and one complete example because the rule is new, then moves through guided use, independent retrieval, and mixed application. Each 15-minute session keeps one action prominent and uses attempts to determine where support is needed.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build a clear model of when and how the product rule works.
sessions.amountLabel: The rule, its parts, and one complete worked example
contentTargets: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating each factor separately and multiplying the results is incorrect.
Apply the rule to a problem closely matching the worked example.

sessions.title: Apply the Rule Step by Step
sessions.objective: Use the product rule with decreasing guidance.
contentTargets: Differentiate products of polynomial functions and simplify the result.
completionEvidence: Solve one product-rule problem using labeled factors and derivatives.
Solve a second problem with only a formula reminder.

sessions.title: Retrieve and Use the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Recall the product rule and carry out the full procedure without prompts.
sessions.amountLabel: One independent derivative plus one error repair
contentTargets: Retrieve and independently execute the product-rule procedure.
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule from memory.
Solve one derivative independently and correct any identified error.

sessions.title: Choose and Apply the Correct Rule
sessions.objective: Distinguish product-rule problems from power-rule problems and solve accurately.
contentTargets: Choose between the product rule and power rule, then justify and apply the choice.
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by the differentiation rule required.
Solve the product-rule items independently and explain each rule choice.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate model, explain the rule in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: It fits a new concept best when you want the big picture first and a concrete example before independent use.
how: Explain the rule in plain language.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix any gap.
methodBriefing.completion: You can state the relationship accurately, repair a gap, and reexplain the rule clearly.
personalization: Use one visible step at a time.
Start with the whole picture, then the steps.
Use a concrete example before the abstract rule.

activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: Product rule idea
activities.body: Study the rule and one example. Keep the example in view while you work.

essentialIdeas: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

activities.label: Explain the rule
activities.title: Explain the product rule
activities.body: In your own words, state what happens to each factor. Keep it short.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is f' times g plus f times g'.
activities.feedback: A complete answer says each factor gets one derivative turn and the results are added. A common gap is to differentiate only one factor or multiply the two derivatives.

activities.label: Repair the mistake
activities.title: Fix the product rule gap
activities.body: Correct the mistake from your last answer and restate the rule once more.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Differentiating each factor separately and multiplying the results is incorrect.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: You do not multiply the derivatives. The derivative of fg is f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: The correction is to add two terms, not to multiply derivatives. A correct repair names both terms and shows that each original factor stays in one term.

activities.label: Reexplain the rule
activities.title: Say it again in plain words
activities.body: Explain the rule again without copying the model. Use a product you choose.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: For a product, take the derivative of the first times the second, then the first times the derivative of the second, and add them.
activities.feedback: This should sound like your own explanation and still keep the two-term structure. If one factor is missing or the derivatives are multiplied, the rule is not yet secure.

activities.label: Choose the right derivative
activities.title: Pick the correct rule
activities.body: Choose the correct derivative of x^2(x+3).
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: The correct choice uses the product rule: derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second. The other choices miss one term or use an unrelated rule.

activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: The product rule
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

activities.label: Explain the rule
activities.title: Explain the product rule
activities.body: In your own words, state what happens to each factor. Keep it short.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is f' times g plus f times g'.
activities.feedback: A complete answer says each factor gets one derivative turn and the results are added. A common gap is to differentiate only one factor or multiply the two derivatives.

activities.label: Repair the mistake
activities.title: Fix the product rule gap
activities.body: Correct the mistake from your last answer and restate the rule once more.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: You do not multiply the derivatives. The derivative of fg is f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: The correction is to add two terms, not to multiply derivatives. A correct repair names both terms and shows that each original factor stays in one term.

activities.label: Reexplain the rule
activities.title: Say it again in plain words
activities.body: Explain the rule again without copying the model. Use a product you choose.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: For a product, take the derivative of the first times the second, then the first times the derivative of the second, and add them.
activities.feedback: This should sound like your own explanation and still keep the two-term structure. If one factor is missing or the derivatives are multiplied, the rule is not yet secure.

activities.label: Choose the right derivative
activities.title: Pick the correct rule
activities.body: Choose the correct derivative of x^2(x+3).
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two functions and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: The correct choice uses the product rule: derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second. The other choices miss one term or use an unrelated rule.
